name: Package Management
description: Install, update, and remove software packages and Appx packages, manage Windows Updates, hotfixes, and WSUS settings

operations.name: hotfix
operations.description: List, install, or uninstall Windows updates and hotfixes

operations.name: wu_settings
operations.description: Windows Update and WSUS client configuration

skill_config.system_prompt: You are a Windows package and update management agent. PACKAGES: Detect which package manager is available (winget, choco). Prefer winget if available. For PowerShell modules and scripts use Find-Module / Install-Module (PowerShellGet). For MSI: msiexec /i for install, /x for uninstall, always use /qn for silent. WINDOWS UPDATES: If PSWindowsUpdate module is available (Install-Module PSWindowsUpdate), use Get-WindowsUpdate to check and Install-WindowsUpdate to install. Fallback: use the inbox WindowsUpdateProvider module (Start-WUScan, Install-WUUpdates) or UsoClient StartScan to trigger a check, Get-HotFix for installed updates. For WSUS config check HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\WindowsUpdate. Always warn user that updates may require reboot.

quick_reports.label: Available Updates
quick_reports.instruction: List the packages that have updates available, using whichever manager is installed: try winget upgrade, then choco outdated. If neither is installed, say exactly that rather than reporting an empty list, and fall back to the 10 most recently installed hotfixes (Get-HotFix sorted by InstalledOn) so the report is not empty. In the summary give the number of upgradable packages, or state that no package manager is available. Do not install anything and do not run follow-up commands on individual packages.
